17-13-0303-C (1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans - Zoning Map Amendment
3909 North Ashland Avenue, Chicago, Illinois

Proposed Zoning: B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District
Lot Area: 4,954 square feet

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant.is seeking a Type I Zoning Map Amendment, with secondary
relief for Administrative Adjustment(s) and/or Variation(s), pursuant to
Section 17-13-0300 of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, in order to permit
the redevelopment of the subject property with a new four-story residential
building. The programming for the proposed new multi-family building
calls for the establishment of a total of eight (8) dwelling units to be
distributed on and between the 1% (ground) through 4" floors. In
consideration of the property’s designation as a Transit Served Location
(TSL), exterior off-street surface parking for three (3) vehicles will be
situated at the rear of the building, with access from the private alley. The
proposed improvements will be masonry in construction and will measure
approximately 41 feet-10 inches in height (4 floor ceiling).

(A) The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 10,104 square feet (2.04 FAR)
(B) The Project’s Density (Lot Area Per Dwelling Unit): 8 units (619.25 square feet)
(C) The amount of off-street parking: *3 automobile spaces; 8 bicycle spaces

* The subject property is located, within 2,640 linear feet of the entrance to the Irving Park Brown
Line (CTA) Train Station, and — therefore, constitutes a designated Transit Served Location (TSL)
under the current Chicago Zoning Ordinance [17-10-0102-B], thereby triggering a distinct
Parking Standard [17-3-0308-B] that limits the maximum allowable off-street residential parking
ratio to 50%. Congruently, the Zoning Ordinance allows for a reduction in the minimum required
off-street parking ratio of more than 50% for a TSL, by and through an Administrative Adjustment
[17-10-0102-B]. The programming for the subject residential development calls for the
establishment of eight (8) new dwelling units at this TSL, which are intended for occupancy by
individuals who work from home or in the immediate neighborhood and/or who predominantly
rely on public transit for commuting and socialization. Applying the TSL Parking Standards
results in a maximum by-right allowance of 4 off-street parking spaces (50%) to serve this
proposed eight-unit building. Due to the irregular shape of the subject site and the unique
topographic conditions encumbering access to the same, the provision of more than three (3)
parking spaces is not feasible and could create undesirable nuisance for the adjacent properties.
Further, the subject property is meaningfully served by both the Brown Line elevated train and
numerous bus lines. Therefore, in a proactive effort to diminish traffic and congestion of on the
shared public streets, the Applicant is seeking an Administrative Adjustment, in conjunction with
this Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment, to further decrease the number of off-street automobile
parking spaces for this transit-served development — from 4 spaces (50%) to 3 spaces (37.5%)

[Section 17-13-1003-EE].

(D) Setbacks: a. *Front Setback: 3 feet-2 inches
b. Rear Setback: 40 feet-3 inches

c. Side Setbacks:
West: 0 feet-3 inches
East: 0 feet-0 inches

* The subject property is located within 2,640 linear feet of the entrance to the Irving Park
(CTA) Train Station, and — therefore, the proposed new development must conform to and
comply with the Pedestrian Street Design Guidelines. [Section 17-3-0504, et seq.] In order to
accommodate having a residential unit on the ground floor and to ensure the privacy and
safety of the residents of the same, the Applicant is seeking an Administrative Adjustment for
relief from the Transparent Window Standards [Section 17-3-0504-C], to permit a reduction
of not more than 25% of the minimum required 60% transparency for the street-facing building
facade. [Section 17-13-1003-P; Section 17-13-1003-Q.]

(E) Building Height: 41 feet-10 inches (underside of 4" Floor ceiling)

COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 17-3-0308
Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations

In all B and C districts, any new construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA or METRA rail
station entrance must satisfy all of the following specific criteria:

1. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B.

The project calls for the construction and occupancy of a new four-story multi-unit
residential development at the subject property, which qualifies as a Transit-Served Location
(TSL) due to its proximity to the Irving Park CTA Brown Line Train Station and its location around
and along multiple designated CTA Bus Line Corridors. The proposed new development will
feature eight (8) dwelling units to be distributed on and between the 1*' (ground) through 4" floors,
which such units are intended for occupancy by individuals who work from home or in the
immediate neighborhood and/or who predominantly rely on public transit for commuting and
socialization. which are intended for occupancy by individuals who work from home or in the
immediate neighborhood and/or who predominantly rely on public transit for commuting and
socialization. The front units on the 2 floor through 4" floors each feature a recessed balcony for
private use and enjoyment of outdoor space. The design and functionality of the dwelling units
were developed in a conscious effort to attract and provide under-resourced economical rental
housing for active residents, many of whom work, play and socialize from their homes, so to ensure
ongoing activation of the property from the ground up and who will patronize and help to revitalize
the existing businesses that comprise this close-knit community. In furthering these same
intentions, the Applicant conscientiously moderated the automobile parking ratio for the new low-
density building, towards contributing to a reduction in the overall traffic and vehicular congestion
in the neighborhood and, in particular, within the shared public streets. At the same time and in
this same vein, the Applicant amplified the amount of onsite bicycle parking so that the residents
of each unit enjoy their own designated space for bicycles and scooters, thereby encouraging
reliance on more carbon-friendly forms of local transportation. Such proposed parking provisions
represent a 37.5% automobile-to-unit ratio and a 100% bicycle-to-unit ratio, thereby providing
parking for the few residents that may own a private vehicle, while still promoting reliance on the
many other meaningful multi-modal forms of nearby public transit and environmentally conscious
transportation. In addition hereto, and in furtherance of these same sustainable policies and goals,
each of the automobile parking spaces will be adapted for EVSE charging.

2. The project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-3-0504, (except
paragraph H if the project is not located along a pedestrian street), pertaining to
pedestrian streets and pedestrian retail streets, even if the project is not located along
a pedestrian street or a pedestrian retail street.

The design for the proposed new multi-unit residential development establishes the entirety
of the street-facing building facade along *Ashland Avenue, including the primary pedestrian
entrance, within 5 feet of the sidewalk, in strict compliance with Section 17-3-0504-B of the
Zoning Ordinance.
